articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 12 published per cycle (56 vs 55 yesterday); 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; the one miss, Latin America at 4%, is a one-day dip from 6% and the last lever tried on it (GAP_COUNTRIES, 2026-09-18) was reverted.
weakestArea: Latin America datelines fell to 4% (about 2 of 56, both Brazil: the Focus inflation survey and the Lagoinha/Banco Master church story), from 6% yesterday, so the region again rests on one country. Science met its 5/day target at 6 but ran 1 against its per-cycle floor of 2 in four of five cycles, with selectors naming barred Scientific Reports/Data papers and methods papers as the remaining supply.
watching: US midterms: voting opened with the Iran war and fuel prices at the top of voters' concerns, and Meta suspended No Kings accounts on Instagram on election day.
Hormuz: US strikes on Qeshm Island and Bandar Lengeh, the IRGC says three tankers hit mines, and Brent climbed back above $105 a day after falling below $104.
Iran-US: Tehran set five conditions for a regional security arrangement in answer to the US ceasefire proposal.
Ukraine-Russia: US-mediated talks are set for Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.
Israel: Trump says US military aid ends with the memorandum at year end, while Israel blocks aid at the Rafah crossing and UNRWA announces mass layoffs over a $70 million shortfall.
ECB: the Bundesbank's Nagel opened the door to a December hike as Eurogroup nominations for Lagarde's successor near their deadline.
Binance: outflows reached $4.7 billion while North Korea denies the FBI-attributed hack, and the proof-of-reserves report is still pending.
South Africa: local elections face ballot-sabotage warnings, and the US suspended South Africa's and Rwanda's AGOA duty-free access.
coverageGaps: GitHub has not received a commit since 2026-11-02 22:03: every cycle's `git pull --rebase` aborts because untracked local content/.ai-models.json and content/.companies.json would be overwritten by origin's 7ad22c80, so master is 36 ahead and 11 behind, and the remote's privacy, about and build.js changes are not in what the cycles deploy. Both files differ from origin's copies, so an operator must pick which version wins before moving them aside.

Science ran under its per-cycle floor (1 of 2) in four of five cycles; Servier's failed muscular-dystrophy trial was the only research result one selector found, and COP17 was filed as science though it is a policy summit (both COP17 copies were then dropped as fuzzy duplicates of yesterday's story).

Economy fell below its post-dedup floor (2 of 3) in two cycles, and one selector found no multi-source economy story at all; the two it later counted each pair a single outlet with one regional source.
Yemen's Saudi-airstrike story rests on Mehr alone, the day's only state-or-advocacy-only article; the selector noted there is no regional Yemeni outlet in the feed.
Pakistan's press-freedom pick had no Pakistani outlet in the feed although Dawn supplied five other stories.
PortWatch series (Taiwan, Panama, Hormuz tanker) timed out again, so the chokepoint figures lean on older snapshots on a day Hormuz led the news.
context: A strong day on output: 56 articles, multi-source up to 38% (from 29%), US datelines at 23%, tech at 16 and no duplicates. The push failure is the item needing action: deploys continue from this box, so readers see new articles, but origin/master is stale and today's cycles cannot pick up the 11 remote commits until the two untracked files are resolved.
